1	# Lesson 0: the big picture
2	
3	Written for Samyak. One of these gets added at each phase.
4	
5	## The problem
6	
7	More and more AI work runs as a team. One lead agent splits a job into pieces and hands each piece to a subagent, a separate copy of the model with its own instructions and its own memory. The subagents work in parallel and report back. Anthropic says its research system used about 15 times the tokens of a normal chat when it worked this way.
8	
9	When a run like that goes wrong or costs too much, it is hard to see why. Questions you can't easily answer today:
10	
11	- Which subagent was told what?
12	- Did two subagents do the same work?
13	- Did two of them disagree, and who won?
14	- Which subagent's work actually made it into the final answer, and which was thrown away?
15	- When a person approved an action, did they have time to look at it?
16	
17	## What already exists
18	
19	Several tools already draw the tree of agents and show how many tokens each one used. Langfuse, Arize Phoenix and Opik have Claude Code plugins; claude-devtools is a free local viewer. Claude Code itself can now report which subagent made each call. So drawing the tree is a solved problem.
20	
21	Nobody I found answers the questions after the tree: what was duplicated, what was used, where agents disagreed, and how approvals happened. Nobody publishes measurements from real runs either. That gap is this project.
22	
23	## What we're building
24	
25	A local tool, `flightrec`, plus a study of my own runs.
26	
27	```
28	transcripts on my Mac → reader → analyzers → viewer + replay → findings → public write-up
29	                        (Phase 1)  (Phase 2)    (Phase 3)       (Phase 4)   (Phase 5)
30	```
31	
32	Like an airplane's flight recorder, it reads what was already recorded and reconstructs what happened. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
33	
34	## Words you'll see a lot
35	
36	- **Transcript:** the file Claude Code writes for each session, one line per event. The format is called JSONL: every line is a small JSON record.
37	- **Lead agent / subagent:** the lead is the agent you talk to. A subagent is a helper the lead starts with the Agent tool. It gets written instructions and reports back.
38	- **Model call (request):** one round trip to the model: send the conversation so far, get a reply. A session is hundreds of these.
39	- **Tokens:** the units models read and write, roughly three quarters of a word each. Input tokens come in three kinds:
40	  - *fresh input*: new text, full price;
41	  - *cache write*: text stored so the next call can reuse it, a bit above full price;
42	  - *cache read*: text reused from that store, a small fraction of the price (one twentieth on Opus 5.5).
43	  Output tokens are what the model writes, including its thinking.
44	- **Tracing / span:** recording each step of a program as a timed block nested inside the step that started it. That nesting is what gives you a tree.
45	- **OpenTelemetry (OTel):** the open standard most tracing tools use to send and store spans.
46	- **Hooks:** small scripts Claude Code runs at moments like "a subagent started" or "permission was requested".
47	- **Lineage:** where a piece of information came from and where it went. Here: did a subagent's report end up in the final answer?
48	
49	## Rules this project runs under
50	
51	- $0. All model work goes through Claude Code on the Pro plan.
52	- My transcripts contain personal data. They stay on my Mac. Snapshots live in `data/`, which git never tracks.
53	- Any public demo uses a run made on purpose for the demo, then redacted, and I approve it first.
54

1	# Lesson 1: reading the black box
2	
3	Written for Samyak after Phase 1 (Nov 23, 2026).
4	
5	## What's in a transcript
6	
7	Every Claude Code session writes `~/.claude/projects/<folder>/<session-id>.jsonl`. Each subagent gets its own file next to it, in `<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, plus a small `.meta.json` that says what kind of agent it was and which tool call started it.
8	
9	The lines that matter most:
10	
11	| Line type | What it holds |
12	|---|---|
13	| `assistant` | part of one model reply: thinking, text, or a tool call, plus the token counts for that call |
14	| `user` | your messages, and the result of each tool call, including the approval decision |
15	| `attachment` | extra context, including reports that background subagents send back |
16	| `cost-state` | Claude Code's own running total of tokens and cost for the session |
17	
18	My history (Aug 27 to Nov 23) spans 21 Claude Code versions. Anthropic's docs say the format is internal and can change on any release. So all format knowledge lives in one file, `src/flightrec/claude_code.py`, with the assumptions written at the top and a test for each.
19	
20	## How the tree is rebuilt
21	
22	The lead starts a subagent with an Agent tool call. That call has an id. The subagent's `.meta.json` stores the same id, and the call's result stores the subagent's id. Matching the two gives an exact parent-to-child link and the instructions the parent wrote. In my 8-subagent session, all 8 linked.
23	
24	## Three traps, and what the reader does about each
25	
26	1. **One call, several lines.** Claude Code writes a reply as one line per piece (thinking, text, each tool call), and every line repeats the token counts. Adding up lines counts the same tokens more than once. The reader groups lines by request id and counts each call once.
27	2. **Copied history.** When a session is forked or resumed, Claude Code copies earlier lines into a new file. As of Nov 23, 1,121 of 4,700 model calls in my history (24%) appear in more than one file. The reader marks those calls as shared, so copied history never counts as new spend.
28	3. **Calls the transcript never shows.** Claude Code makes some model calls that are never written to the transcript. See below.
29	
30	## How we know the reader is right
31	
32	Claude Code keeps its own running total per session. I compared the reader's totals with it for every session, model by model.
33	
34	A fair comparison only works on "clean" sessions: no copied history, never compacted, not still running. The rule for those: the reader may count *less* than Claude Code (some calls aren't in the transcript), but it must never count *more*. Counting more would mean a double-counting bug.
35	
36	Results across my 113 sessions (76 with Claude Code totals, 42 clean):
37	
38	- **0 overcounts.** The reader never counted a token Claude Code didn't.
39	- **17 exact matches**, to the token, on every model.
40	- **25 sessions where the transcript is missing calls.** Each missing call looks the same: about 506 fresh input tokens, a read of the cached conversation, and a reply of about 20 tokens. There are 1 to 14 per session. Together they are 9.14M of 50.47M tokens in those sessions (18.1%), almost all of it cheap cache reads. I tested five explanations (the auto-mode safety check, the advisor tool, multi-step calls, session naming, idle recaps) and none fit. They are an open question. Claude Code's OpenTelemetry export labels each call with its purpose, so that's the next place to look.
41	- **Calls on models the transcript never shows:** 1.40M of 92.27M tokens (1.5%), all on Haiku, in 6 sessions. These are Claude Code's own side jobs.
42	
43	## Tokens are not dollars
44	
45	The hidden calls are 18% of the tokens in those sessions, but most of them are cache reads, which cost a twentieth of fresh input. A finding can look big in tokens and small in money, or the other way round. The write-up will always say which one it means.
46	
47	## What the reader can't see (so far)
48	
49	- Calls Claude Code makes without writing them down (above).
50	- The summarizing call behind each compaction.
51	- Approvals in sessions from older versions, which didn't record them.
52	- Subagents that left no transcript file. They appear in the tree as stubs, with their instructions but no token counts.
53

1	# Lesson 2: what a token costs, and where the work went
2	
3	Written for Samyak after Phase 2 (Nov 23, 2026). Numbers are from my own transcripts on that date; they move a little as new sessions are written.
4	
5	## Turning tokens into dollars
6	
7	Tokens of different kinds cost very different amounts, so token counts alone can mislead. To compare fairly I needed each model's price per token type. I didn't copy a price list. Claude Code saves its own dollar cost next to its token counts, so I worked backwards from those records.
8	
9	The published list prices fit. For Opus 5.5, per million tokens: $4 fresh input, $5 for a 5-minute cache write, $8 for a 1-hour cache write, $0.20 for a cache read, $20 for output. They reproduce Claude Code's recorded cost to the cent in 37 of 38 Opus records that split cache writes by duration. The one miss costs 1.8 times the prediction, which looks like fast mode (twice the price). Priced call by call, the reader's totals match Claude Code's to the cent in all 12 clean sessions where every model has a known price.
10	
11	I pay a flat Pro fee, so these dollars are "what the API would charge". They are a fair way to weigh a cheap cache read against an expensive output token, not a bill.
12	
13	## How big is a tool result, in tokens?
14	
15	Transcripts store tool results as text. Between two calls of the same agent, the input grows by exactly what was added. When exactly one tool result arrived in between, that growth is the result's size in tokens. Across 835 such steps in my history:
16	
17	- command output (Bash): about 2.05 characters per token
18	- file reads: about 2.44
19	- all tools together: about 2.02
20	
21	The usual rule of thumb is 4 characters per token. That holds for plain English. Code, file listings and line-numbered output pack fewer characters per token. Estimating with 4 would understate tool output by about 40%. Screenshots carry no text, so their size can't be measured this way; the tool says so.
22	
23	## Carried cost: why early reads cost more
24	
25	Every model call in an agent loop resends the whole conversation. Anything added to an agent's context is written to the cache once and then read back on every later call. So a tool result's real cost is its size times (one cache write plus one cache read per later call). A large file read on step 2 of a 60-step agent is paid for 59 more times. This assumes the content stays in context; Claude Code can clear old results, so carried numbers are an upper bound.
26	
27	## What the analyzers found across my 11 multi-agent sessions
28	
29	These are first results, not the study.
30	
31	- **Total:** about $162 API-equivalent. Subagents were 16% of it.
32	- **Startup cost:** a subagent starts with a median of 48k tokens of context before it does anything: system prompt, tool list, memory files, its instructions. Across all subagents that base context is 23% of their cost. For small jobs it dominates. In one session, each of 8 subagents started with about 42k tokens and ran only 4 or 5 calls, so the base context was 68 to 83% of each one's cost.
33	- **Repeated work:** zero repeats inside a single agent. Sixteen times one agent read a file another had already read, all of them file reads, at most $0.77 (0.5% of cost). For my runs, re-reading files is a small cost.
34	- **Where subagent work went** (30 subagents): 22 used, 4 unclear, 2 left a file nobody else touched, 2 with no trace found. (A first count said 33; forks carry copies of their source's subagents, so 3 were counted twice. Until Phase 4 the reader also dropped reports from background subagents, which made 2 look like they never reported; see what-went-wrong.)
35	- **File conflicts:** none. No two agents wrote the same file.
36	- **Approvals:** in the calls these sessions made themselves, a person decided none of about 1,660 permission decisions. Settings decided all of them. (A first count said 1 of 2,029; that one human decision was a copy from an older file.)
37	
38	## How "used" is decided, and how much to trust it
39	
40	Work comes back two ways, so lineage checks both:
41	
42	1. **The report.** Does text from the subagent's final report show up in what its parent wrote afterwards? It looks for distinctive items: URLs, file paths, numbers, and name-shaped words like `SubagentStop` or `claude-devtools`. It ignores anything the parent already had.
43	2. **Files.** If the subagent wrote a file, did another agent read it, use it in a command, edit it, or write over it?
44	
45	I tested it on the one run where I know the answer: the planning session for this project. Three research helpers reported back and I used all three, in my own words. The first version, which matched URLs, paths, numbers and phrases, called only 1 of the 3 "used". Adding names fixed it: 3 of 3.
46	
47	Three known answers is a thin test, so I checked it against a model.
48	
49	### Checking the checker
50	
51	`scripts/judge_lineage.py` asks Haiku, once per subagent report, whether the lead's later work relied on it. Haiku sees the instructions, the report, a little of what the lead wrote before, and the next 60,000 characters of what the lead did after. It never sees my verdict. Mixed in are 6 controls: a report shown next to a lead from a different session, where the right answer has to be "not used".
52	
53	18 reports qualified at the time. (In Phase 4 I found the reader had been dropping reports from background subagents; with that fixed, 30 of 30 subagents have a report, so 12 more await the same check.) The run took 24 calls, about 3 minutes, and 680k Haiku tokens, about $0.12 at API prices, on my Pro plan.
54	
55	| My verdict | Haiku said | Reading |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| used (9) | relied 8, partly 1 | Agree in all 9. |
58	| some trace (4) | relied 3, partly 1 | Haiku says used. One case shows real use my matcher underrated. |
59	| no trace found (5) | relied 3, partly 2 | Disagree in all 5. See below. |
60	| controls (6) | not used 6 | Haiku right in all 6. My matcher said "some trace" on 2 of them. |
61	
62	Neither side is ground truth, so I checked Haiku's evidence without reading it. For each case, the script takes the names, numbers and longer words Haiku cites, keeps the ones found in both the report and the lead's later work, and asks whether the lead already had them before the report arrived. When both methods say "used", 1 to 7 cited items are new. In 4 of the 5 "no trace found" cases, every item Haiku cites was already in the lead's earlier work. Haiku was crediting the report with things the lead already knew, even though the prompt told it not to. Four of those five are from one session where 8 helpers did similar jobs in parallel, so the lead had already seen the same content from a sibling.
63	
64	Haiku's confidence lined up with this in the first round: all 6 of its confidence-5 verdicts had at least one new item, and its confidence-3 verdicts had at most one.
65	
66	### Second round (Phase 4)
67	
68	After fixing the reader (it had been dropping reports from background subagents), 12 more reports existed. I ran them and 6 new controls, named after their pairs so they can't drift. Across all 30 reports and 12 controls:
69	
70	- Where text matching says "used", Haiku agreed in 15 of 15.
71	- Haiku said "not used" on all 12 mismatched controls. Text matching gave a weak "unclear" on 3 of them.
72	- Where text matching found no trace in the report (8), Haiku said used in all 8. In 7, nothing Haiku cited was new to the lead: 5 were things the lead already had, at confidence 4 or below, and 2 were "recommendation followed", where the lead did what the report advised in its own words. Text can't show that kind of use.
73	- The confidence pattern from round 1 broke: 3 confidence-5 verdicts had no new items, all of them "recommendation followed". Confidence is a hint, not a test.
74	- By cost the two methods barely differ: 96% of subagent spend reached the lead by text matching plus files, 100% by Haiku. They disagree only on $1.07 of $25.90.
75	
76	What changed in the tool:
77	
78	- **"used" stays.** A model agreed in 9 of 9.
79	- **"some trace" is now "unclear".** A single matching item or a little shared phrasing also happened by chance in 2 of 6 mismatched pairs, so it can't tell use from coincidence.
80	- **"no trace found" stays, with a clearer meaning:** nothing new from the report reached the later work. The lead may still have read it and found nothing it didn't already have, which is its own kind of waste when helpers run in parallel on overlapping jobs.
81	
82	Limits: 18 real cases, 8 from one session. A model judge is not ground truth either; it over-credits shared topics. Text matching misses use that leaves no names or numbers behind, such as a recommendation followed in different words.
83	
84	## Words
85	
86	- **Least squares:** a way to find the numbers that best fit many equations at once. Here, the prices that best explain many recorded costs.
87	- **Fingerprint (hash):** a short code computed from content. Identical content always gives the same code, and different content almost never does.
88	- **Carried cost:** what a piece of context costs over the rest of an agent's life, because it is re-read on every later call.
89	- **Lineage:** where a piece of work went after it was produced.
90	- **Control:** a case where the right answer is known in advance (here, "not used"), mixed in to catch a method that says yes too easily.
91	- **Blind:** the judge doesn't see the answer it is being compared with.
92

1	# Lesson 3: the viewer
2	
3	Written for Samyak after Phase 3 (Nov 23, 2026).
4	
5	## What it is
6	
7	`flightrec view <session>` writes one HTML file for a run. Open it in any browser. The file holds everything: the run's data, the drawing code and the styles. It needs no server, loads nothing from the internet, and keeps working if you move or email it. `flightrec view --all` writes a page per multi-agent run plus an index page that lists them.
8	
9	## How it's built
10	
11	Python reads the transcripts and runs the analyzers, as in Phases 1 and 2. A new module, `view.py`, turns the results into a **payload**: one bundle of plain data (agents, model calls, tool calls, findings, times) for the page to draw. The payload is pasted into a template page, `viewer.html`. When the page opens, a few hundred lines of plain JavaScript draw the timeline as **SVG**, the browser's built-in format for shapes and lines. There are no libraries, so there is nothing to download and nothing that can change under it.
12	
13	All transcript text is inserted into the page as plain text, never as HTML. If a transcript contains something that looks like code (a report quoting `<script>`, say), it shows up as text and can't run. A unit test checks this.
14	
15	## Reading a page
16	
17	- **One lane per agent.** The lead is on top; each subagent sits under the agent that started it. Purple bars above the line are model calls; taller means more context was sent. Green bars below the line are tool calls; orange ones started a subagent; red ones failed.
18	- **The gray first bar** on a subagent lane is its first model call. That call carries the base context every subagent starts with (system prompt, tool list, memory, instructions), which Lesson 2 found is about a quarter of subagent cost.
19	- **Dashed orange lines** show a subagent being started. **Arrows** show its report coming back, colored by lineage: green used, amber unclear, gray no trace.
20	- **Gray bands** are idle time. Any gap over 10 minutes is squeezed into a narrow band labeled with its real length. One of my runs spans 13 days but was active for 5 hours 17 minutes; without squeezing, the work would be a few slivers on an empty screen.
21	- **Replay.** Play moves a playhead through the run; what hasn't happened yet is faded. The counters show cost, tokens and agents running as of the playhead. The arrow keys step from one event to the next. "At the playhead" lists the latest events: tool calls with their file, command or URL, model calls with their size, and what each agent wrote.
22	- **Findings** sit on the lanes as small triangles and in a list you can filter: startup cost, repeated work (selecting one draws a link back to the first time), subagent lineage, file conflicts, and your approvals. Clicking one jumps the playhead there.
23	- **Zoom.** Parallel subagents often all run inside one minute of a long session. "Zoom to its time" on a selected agent fits its work to the screen.
24	
25	## What it can't show
26	
27	Tool results are not stored, only their size, so the replay shows what an agent did and how big the answer was, not the answer. Calls Claude Code never writes to the transcript (Lesson 1) are missing from the lanes. Costs are API-equivalent.
28	
29	## Words
30	
31	- **Self-contained page:** a single file that carries everything it needs to display.
32	- **Payload:** the data handed to the page, here as JSON (a plain text format for lists and labelled values).
33	- **SVG:** a way to describe drawings (rectangles, lines, text) that browsers render directly.
34	- **Playhead:** the marker for "now" in a replay.

1	"""Adapter for Claude Code transcripts.
2	
3	This is the only file that knows Claude Code's on-disk format. Claude Code's
4	docs say the format is internal and can change on any release, so every
5	assumption is listed here and checked by the tests.
6	
7	Assumptions (checked against Claude Code 2.1.168 to 2.1.330, Aug-Nov 2026):
8	
9	Layout
10	  <root>/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl                          the lead agent
11	  <root>/<project>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl     one subagent
12	  <root>/<project>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json its type, description,
13	      the id of the tool call that started it (toolUseId), and spawnDepth
14	
15	Model calls
16	  One model call is written as several "assistant" lines, one per content
17	  block (thinking, text, tool use), sharing one requestId. Each line repeats
18	  the call's token usage; only output_tokens can grow from line to line. So we
19	  group by requestId and take the field-wise maximum.
20	  Lines with model "<synthetic>" are placeholders Claude Code writes itself.
21	  No model call happened, so we skip them.
22	
23	Tool calls and approvals
24	  A tool call is a "tool_use" block in an assistant line. Its result is a
25	  "tool_result" block in a later "user" line. That user line may carry
26	  permissionDecision = {decision, source}; source "config" means settings or
27	  the permission mode allowed it, "user_*" means a person clicked.
28	
29	Subagents
30	  The parent starts a subagent with an Agent (formerly Task) tool call.
31	  Its result carries toolUseResult.agentId. Synchronous subagents
32	  (status "completed") return their report in that result. Background ones
33	  (status "async_launched") deliver it later in a line whose origin has
34	  kind "peer" and from = the subagent's id.
35	
36	Messages from the person
37	  User lines with origin.kind "human". Older versions have no origin, so a
38	  plain user line that is not a tool result counts as a human message.
39	
40	Other records
41	  cost-state      Claude Code's own running token and cost totals for the session
42	  derived-from    which session this one was forked, resumed or cleared from
43	  system/compact_boundary   a compaction (the conversation was summarized)
44	"""
45	
46	from __future__ import annotations
47	
48	import hashlib
49	import json
50	import os
51	from datetime import datetime
52	from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
53	
54	from .model import Agent, Approval, Event, Request, Run, ToolCall, Usage
55	
56	# Tool-input fields that carry text the agent wrote (used to trace where reports went).
57	WRITTEN_FIELDS = ("content", "new_string", "command", "prompt", "query", "url", "description")
58	
59	SPAWN_TOOLS = ("Agent", "Task")
60	SYNTHETIC_MODEL = "<synthetic>"
61	
62	# Record types we read, or have looked at and deliberately ignore.
63	# Anything else is counted in Run.unknown_record_types so format drift shows up.
64	KNOWN_TYPES = {
65	    "assistant", "user", "attachment", "system", "cost-state", "derived-from",
66	    "custom-title", "ai-title", "summary", "queue-operation", "last-prompt",
67	    "atis-latch", "agent-name", "file-history-snapshot", "file-history-delta",
68	    "api-request", "api-request-blob", "api-request-shape", "data-flow-records",
69	    "data-flow-incomplete", "mode", "permission-mode", "artifact-autoreact-ledger",
70	    "frame-link", "relocated", "bridge-session", "tools-used",
71	    "artifact-comment-monitor", "pr-link",
72	}
73	
74	
75	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- files
76	
77	def default_root() -> str:
78	    base = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR") or os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".claude")
79	    return os.path.join(base, "projects")
80	
81	
82	def find_sessions(root: Optional[str] = None) -> List[str]:
83	    """Every lead-agent transcript under root."""
84	    root = root or default_root()
85	    out = []
86	    for project in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
87	        pdir = os.path.join(root, project)
88	        if not os.path.isdir(pdir):
89	            continue
90	        for name in sorted(os.listdir(pdir)):
91	            if name.endswith(".jsonl"):
92	                out.append(os.path.join(pdir, name))
93	    return out
94	
95	
96	def subagent_files(session_path: str) -> List[str]:
97	    sub = os.path.join(session_path[: -len(".jsonl")], "subagents")
98	    if not os.path.isdir(sub):
99	        return []
100	    return [
101	        os.path.join(sub, n)
102	        for n in sorted(os.listdir(sub))
103	        if n.startswith("agent-") and n.endswith(".jsonl")
104	    ]
105

107	def session_id_of(path: str) -> str:

169	    """The readable text in a message or tool-result content."""

172	    if isinstance(content, list):
173	        parts = []

204	class _Links:
205	    """Facts gathered while reading, joined up after every file is read."""
206	
207	    def __init__(self) -> None:
208	        self.spawn_results: Dict[str, Tuple[ToolCall, dict, Optional[datetime], str]] = {}

214	def _read_agent(records: List[dict], agent: Agent, run: Run, links: _Links) -> None:
215	    is_lead = agent.id == "main"
216	    groups: Dict[str, List[Tuple[dict, Optional[datetime]]]] = {}
217	    order: List[str] = []
218	    calls: Dict[str, ToolCall] = {}
219	
220	    for r in records:
221	        rtype = r.get("type")
222	        ts = parse_ts(r.get("timestamp"))
223	        if rtype not in KNOWN_TYPES:
224	            run.unknown_record_types[str(rtype)] += 1
225	        if r.get("version"):
226	            run.versions.add(r["version"])
227	
228	        if rtype == "assistant":
229	            msg = r.get("message") or {}
230	            if msg.get("model") == SYNTHETIC_MODEL:
231	                continue
232	            agent.seen(ts)
233	            rid = r.get("requestId") or msg.get("id") or r.get("uuid") or f"line-{len(order)}"
234	            if rid not in groups:
235	                groups[rid] = []
236	                order.append(rid)
237	                agent.events.append(Event("call", ts, rid))
238	            groups[rid].append((r, ts))
239	            for b in msg.get("content") or []:
240	                if not isinstance(b, dict):
241	                    continue
242	                if b.get("type") == "text" and b.get("text"):
243	                    agent.outputs.append((ts, b["text"]))
244	                    agent.said.append((ts, b["text"]))
245	                if b.get("type") == "tool_use" and b.get("id") not in calls:
246	                    inp = b.get("input") if isinstance(b.get("input"), dict) else {}
247	                    calls[b["id"]] = ToolCall(
248	                        id=b["id"],
249	                        agent_id=agent.id,
250	                        request_id=rid,
251	                        name=b.get("name") or "?",
252	                        input=inp,

254	                    )

256	                    if written:

259	        elif rtype == "user":
260	            agent.seen(ts)
261	            _read_user_line(r, ts, agent, run, calls, links)
262	
263	        elif rtype == "attachment":
264	            origin = (r.get("attachment") or {}).get("origin")
265	            size = -1
266	            if isinstance(origin, dict) and is_lead:
267	                if origin.get("kind") == "peer":
268	                    links.deliveries.append((origin, ts))
269	                    size = len(str(origin.get("handbackReportText") or origin.get("body") or ""))
270	                elif origin.get("kind") == "human":
271	                    run.human_messages.append(ts)
272	            agent.events.append(Event("context", ts, None, size))
273	
274	        elif rtype == "system" and is_lead and r.get("subtype") == "compact_boundary":
275	            run.compactions.append(ts)
276	        elif rtype == "cost-state" and is_lead:
277	            run.reported_totals = r
278	        elif rtype == "derived-from" and is_lead:
279	            run.derived_from.extend(s for s in (r.get("sessions") or []) if isinstance(s, dict))
280	        elif rtype == "custom-title" and is_lead and r.get("customTitle"):
281	            run.title = r["customTitle"]
282	
283	    for rid in order:
284	        lines = groups[rid]

289	            usage = usage.max_with(usage_of(msg))
290	            for b in msg.get("content") or []:
291	                if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_use" and b.get("id"):

295	        agent.requests.append(
296	            Request(
297	                id=rid,
298	                agent_id=agent.id,
299	                model=last.get("model") or "?",
300	                started=min(times) if times else None,
301	                ended=max(times) if times else None,
302	                usage=usage,
303	                stop_reason=last.get("stop_reason"),
304	                tool_use_ids=tool_ids,
305	                speed=(last.get("usage") or {}).get("speed"),
306	            )

311	def _read_user_line(r: dict, ts, agent: Agent, run: Run, calls: Dict[str, ToolCall], links: _Links) -> None:
312	    msg = r.get("message") or {}
313	    content = msg.get("content")
314	    results = []
315	    if isinstance(content, list):
316	        results = [b for b in content if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_result"]
317	
318	    if results:
319	        decision = r.get("permissionDecision")
320	        result_meta = r.get("toolUseResult")
321	        for b in results:
322	            call = calls.get(b.get("tool_use_id"))
323	            body = text_of(b.get("content"))
324	            agent.events.append(Event("result", ts, b.get("tool_use_id"), len(body)))
325	            if call is None:
326	                continue  # a result whose call we never saw, e.g. history copied without it
327	            call.finished = ts
328	            call.is_error = bool(b.get("is_error"))
329	            call.result_chars = len(body)
330	            raw = b.get("content")
331	            call.result_media = isinstance(raw, list) and any(
332	                isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") in ("image", "document") for x in raw)
333	            if call.result_media:
334	                call.result_hash = fingerprint(json.dumps(raw, sort_keys=True, default=str))
335	            elif body:
336	                call.result_hash = fingerprint(body)
337	            else:
338	                call.result_hash = None  # empty result: nothing to compare
339	            if isinstance(decision, dict) and decision.get("decision"):
340	                call.approval = Approval(
341	                    tool_use_id=call.id,
342	                    decision=str(decision.get("decision")),
343	                    source=str(decision.get("source") or "unknown"),
344	                    reason=decision.get("reasonType") or decision.get("reasonCode"),

348	                links.spawn_results[str(result_meta["agentId"])] = (call, result_meta, ts, body)

351	    agent.events.append(Event("context", ts, None, text_len(content)))
352	    if agent.id != "main":

354	    origin = r.get("origin")
355	    # A background subagent's report arrives as a "peer" message. Claude Code marks it
356	    # isMeta (not typed by a person), so check for it before skipping meta records.
357	    if isinstance(origin, dict) and origin.get("kind") == "peer":
358	        links.deliveries.append((origin, ts))

371	def parse_session(path: str) -> Run:
372	    """Read a lead transcript and all its subagents into one Run."""
373	    run = Run(session_id=session_id_of(path), path=path, project=os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path)))
374	    links = _Links()
375	
376	    lead = Agent(id="main", parent_id=None, kind="lead", transcript=path)
377	    run.agents["main"] = lead
378	    records, bad = read_jsonl(path)
379	    run.bad_lines += bad
380	    _read_agent(records, lead, run, links)
381	
382	    for sub_path in subagent_files(path):
383	        agent_id = os.path.basename(sub_path)[len("agent-"): -len(".jsonl")]
384	        meta = _read_json(sub_path[: -len(".jsonl")] + ".meta.json")
385	        agent = Agent(

389	            description=str(meta.get("description") or ""),
390	            model_requested=meta.get("model"),
391	            spawn_tool_use_id=meta.get("toolUseId"),
392	            transcript=sub_path,

394	        run.agents[agent_id] = agent
395	        records, bad = read_jsonl(sub_path)
396	        run.bad_lines += bad
397	        _read_agent(records, agent, run, links)
398	
399	    _link(run, links)
400	    return run

403	def _link(run: Run, links: _Links) -> None:
404	    owner = {c.id: a.id for a in run.agents.values() for c in a.tool_calls}

406	
407	    # 1. Subagents that left a transcript: find the call that started them.
408	    for agent in run.subagents:

410	        if call is None:

414	        agent.parent_id = owner[call.id]
415	        call.spawned_agent_id = agent.id
416	        agent.instructions = str(call.input.get("prompt") or "")
417	        agent.description = agent.description or str(call.input.get("description") or "")
418	        if "run_in_background" in call.input:
419	            agent.background = bool(call.input.get("run_in_background"))
420	
421	    # 2. Spawn results: background vs synchronous, reports, and subagents with no transcript.
422	    for agent_id, (call, meta, ts, body) in links.spawn_results.items():
423	        agent = run.agents.get(agent_id)
424	        if agent is None:
425	            agent = Agent(
426	                id=agent_id,
427	                parent_id=call.agent_id,
428	                kind=str(meta.get("agentType") or call.input.get("subagent_type") or "unknown"),
429	                description=str(call.input.get("description") or meta.get("description") or ""),
430	                instructions=str(call.input.get("prompt") or meta.get("prompt") or ""),
431	                spawn_tool_use_id=call.id,

436	            run.missing_transcripts.append(agent_id)
437	        call.spawned_agent_id = agent_id
438	        status = meta.get("status")
439	        if status == "async_launched" or meta.get("isAsync"):

441	        elif status == "completed":

444	            if agent.report_at is None:
445	                agent.report_at = ts

447	                agent.report_text = body
448	
449	    # 3. Background reports delivered later as "peer" messages.
450	    for origin, ts in links.deliveries:
451	        sender = str(origin.get("from") or "")

1	"""Analyzers: turn a Run into findings.
2	
3	Every number here comes from the transcript. Where we estimate (token size of
4	a tool result, carried cost), the method is written next to the code and in
5	docs/learn/02-what-a-token-costs.md.
6	
7	Carried cost: in an agent loop every model call resends the whole
8	conversation. Anything added to an agent's context is written to the prompt
9	cache once and then read back on every later call of that agent. So a tool
10	result's real cost is
11	
12	    size x (cache-write price  +  later calls x cache-read price)
13	
14	This assumes the content stays in context until the agent stops. Claude Code
15	can clear old tool results or compact the conversation, so treat carried
16	numbers as an upper bound.
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import json
22	import re
23	import statistics
24	from collections import Counter, defaultdict
25	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
26	from datetime import datetime, timedelta
27	from typing import Dict, Iterable, Iterator, List, Optional, Set, Tuple
28	
29	from .model import Agent, Run, ToolCall, Usage
30	from .pricing import PRICES, request_cost, usage_cost
31	
32	DEFAULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 2.0  # median measured on the author's transcripts (Nov 2026); calibrate() replaces it
33	
34	
35	def _ts(t: Optional[datetime]) -> float:
36	    return t.timestamp() if t else 0.0
37	
38	
39	def main_model(agent: Agent) -> Optional[str]:
40	    models = Counter(r.model for r in agent.requests)
41	    return models.most_common(1)[0][0] if models else None
42	
43	
44	def write_price(agent: Agent) -> float:
45	    """Average cache-write price for this agent, weighted by its 5-minute / 1-hour mix."""
46	    p = PRICES.get(main_model(agent) or "")
47	    if not p:
48	        return 0.0
49	    u = agent.usage()
50	    share_1h = (u.cache_write_1h / u.cache_write) if u.cache_write else 0.0
51	    return p[1] * (1 - share_1h) + p[2] * share_1h
52	
53	
54	def read_price(agent: Agent) -> float:
55	    p = PRICES.get(main_model(agent) or "")
56	    return p[3] if p else 0.0
57	
58	
59	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- token size of tool results
60	
61	@dataclass
62	class TokenScale:
63	    """Characters per token, measured per tool from the transcripts themselves."""
64	
65	    by_tool: Dict[str, float]
66	    overall: float
67	    samples: int
68	
69	    def ratio(self, tool: str) -> float:
70	        return self.by_tool.get(tool, self.overall)
71	
72	    def tokens(self, call: ToolCall) -> int:
73	        return int(round(call.result_chars / self.ratio(call.name)))
74	
75	
76	def one_result_steps(agent: Agent) -> Iterator[Tuple[str, int, int]]:
77	    """(tool name, result chars, tokens added) for every step where exactly one
78	    tool result, and nothing else, arrived between two calls of the same model."""
79	    reqs = {r.id: r for r in agent.requests}
80	    calls = {c.id: c for c in agent.tool_calls}
81	    prev, between = None, []
82	    for ev in agent.events:
83	        if ev.kind != "call":
84	            between.append(ev)
85	            continue
86	        if prev and len(between) == 1 and between[0].kind == "result" and between[0].chars >= 200:
87	            a, b, c = reqs.get(prev), reqs.get(ev.ref or ""), calls.get(between[0].ref or "")
88	            if a and b and c and a.model == b.model:
89	                added = b.usage.total_input - a.usage.total_input - a.usage.output
90	                if added > 0:
91	                    yield c.name, between[0].chars, added
92	        prev, between = ev.ref, []
93	
94	
95	def calibrate(runs: Iterable[Run], min_samples: int = 10) -> TokenScale:
96	    per_tool: Dict[str, List[float]] = defaultdict(list)
97	    for run in runs:
98	        for agent in run.agents.values():
99	            for name, chars, tokens in one_result_steps(agent):
100	                per_tool[name].append(chars / tokens)
101	    every = [x for v in per_tool.values() for x in v]
102	    overall = statistics.median(every) if every else DEFAULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN
103	    by_tool = {k: statistics.median(v) for k, v in per_tool.items() if len(v) >= min_samples}
104	    return TokenScale(by_tool, overall, len(every))
105	
106	
107	def later_calls(agent: Agent) -> Dict[str, int]:
108	    """For each tool result: how many model calls this agent made after it arrived."""
109	    remaining = sum(1 for e in agent.events if e.kind == "call")
110	    out: Dict[str, int] = {}
111	    for e in agent.events:
112	        if e.kind == "call":
113	            remaining -= 1
114	        elif e.kind == "result" and e.ref and e.ref not in out:
115	            out[e.ref] = remaining
116	    return out

119	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 1. repeated work

121	def target(call: ToolCall) -> Optional[str]:
122	    """What a read-like tool call looked at. None for tools that change things."""
123	    i = call.input
124	    if call.name == "Read":
125	        return f"file {i.get('file_path')} {i.get('offset', '')}:{i.get('limit', '')}"
126	    if call.name == "WebFetch":
127	        return f"page {i.get('url')}"
128	    if call.name == "WebSearch":
129	        return f"search {str(i.get('query', '')).strip().lower()}"
130	    if call.name == "Bash":
131	        return f"command {str(i.get('command', '')).strip()}"
132	    if call.name in ("Grep", "Glob", "LS", "NotebookRead"):
133	        return f"{call.name.lower()} {json.dumps(i, sort_keys=True)}"
134	    return None
135

137	@dataclass
138	class Repeat:
139	    call: ToolCall
140	    first: ToolCall
141	    within_agent: bool  # True: this agent already had the identical result
142	    tokens: int
143	    later_calls: int
144	    cost: float  # API-equivalent: one cache write plus a cache read per later call
145	
146	    @property
147	    def carried_tokens(self) -> int:
148	        return self.tokens * (1 + self.later_calls)
149	
150	
151	def find_repeats(run: Run, scale: TokenScale) -> List[Repeat]:
152	    later = {a.id: later_calls(a) for a in run.agents.values()}
153	    holders: Dict[Tuple[str, str], Set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
154	    first_of: Dict[Tuple[str, str], ToolCall] = {}
155	    out = []
156	    calls = [c for c in run.tool_calls() if c.result_hash and not c.is_error and target(c)]
157	    calls.sort(key=lambda c: _ts(c.finished or c.started))
158	    for c in calls:
159	        key = (target(c) or "", c.result_hash or "")
160	        if key not in first_of:
161	            first_of[key] = c
162	            holders[key].add(c.agent_id)
163	            continue
164	        agent = run.agents[c.agent_id]
165	        n_later = later[c.agent_id].get(c.id, 0)
166	        tokens = 0 if c.result_media else scale.tokens(c)  # image/document size can't be measured from text
167	        cost = tokens * (write_price(agent) + n_later * read_price(agent)) / 1e6
168	        out.append(Repeat(c, first_of[key], c.agent_id in holders[key], tokens, n_later, cost))
169	        holders[key].add(c.agent_id)
170	    return out
171	
172	
173	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2. startup cost
174	
175	@dataclass
176	class Startup:
177	    agent: Agent
178	    first_input: int  # tokens in the first call's input: system prompt, tools, memory, instructions
179	    calls: int
180	    total_input: int
181	    carried_cost: float  # cost of that base context across all of the agent's calls
182	    total_cost: float
183	
184	    @property
185	    def token_share(self) -> float:
186	        return min(1.0, self.first_input * self.calls / self.total_input) if self.total_input else 0.0
187	
188	    @property
189	    def cost_share(self) -> float:
190	        return min(1.0, self.carried_cost / self.total_cost) if self.total_cost else 0.0
191	
192	
193	def startup_costs(run: Run) -> List[Startup]:
194	    out = []
195	    for agent, _ in run.tree():
196	        reqs = sorted(agent.requests, key=lambda r: _ts(r.started))
197	        if not reqs:
198	            continue
199	        first = reqs[0]
200	        first_in = first.usage.total_input
201	        input_only = Usage(input=first.usage.input, cache_write=first.usage.cache_write,
202	                           cache_read=first.usage.cache_read, cache_write_1h=first.usage.cache_write_1h)
203	        first_cost = usage_cost(input_only, first.model, first.speed) or 0.0
204	        carried = first_cost + (len(reqs) - 1) * first_in * read_price(agent) / 1e6
205	        total = sum(usage_cost(r.usage, r.model, r.speed) or 0.0 for r in reqs)
206	        out.append(Startup(agent, first_in, len(reqs), sum(r.usage.total_input for r in reqs), carried, total))
207	    return out
208	
209	
210	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3. lineage
211	
212	URL_RE = re.compile(r"https?://[^\s)\]>\"'`|,]+")
213	PATH_RE = re.compile(r"(?:~|/)[\w.\-/]*\w\.\w{1,6}\b")
214	NUM_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?%?(?![\w])")
215	WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+")
216	# Name-shaped words survive paraphrase: CamelCase (SubagentStop), acronyms (MAST),
217	# and hyphen/underscore compounds (claude-devtools, parent_agent_id).
218	NAME_RE = re.compile(
219	    r"(?<![\w/.-])(?:[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)+|[A-Z][a-z0-9]+(?:[A-Z][a-z0-9]*)+|[A-Z]{3,}s?)(?![\w/-])"
220	)
221	SHINGLE = 6
222	
223	
224	def signals(text: str) -> Set[str]:
225	    """Distinctive items: URLs, file paths, names, and numbers unlikely to repeat by chance."""
226	    items = {u.rstrip(".") for u in URL_RE.findall(text)}
227	    text = URL_RE.sub(" ", text)  # so pieces of a URL aren't counted again as paths or names
228	    items |= set(PATH_RE.findall(text))
229	    items |= set(NAME_RE.findall(text))
230	    for n in NUM_RE.findall(text):
231	        digits = re.sub(r"\D", "", n)
232	        if len(digits) >= 3 and not re.fullmatch(r"(19|20)\d\d", n):
233	            items.add(n)
234	    return items
235	
236	
237	def shingles(text: str) -> Set[Tuple[str, ...]]:
238	    words = WORD_RE.findall(text.lower())
239	    return {tuple(words[i:i + SHINGLE]) for i in range(len(words) - SHINGLE + 1)}
240	
241	
242	@dataclass
243	class Lineage:
244	    """Where a subagent's work went. Two channels:
245	
246	    report  does text from its final report (URLs, paths, numbers, exact
247	            phrases the parent didn't already have) show up in what the parent
248	            wrote afterwards?
249	    files   what happened to files it wrote: another agent read them or used
250	            them in a command (picked up), edited them (revised), or wrote over
251	            them (replaced)?
252	    """
253	
254	    agent: Agent
255	    status: str
256	    report_status: str = "no report"  # used / unclear / no trace found / no report / arrived after parent stopped
257	    items_total: int = 0
258	    items_reused: int = 0
259	    phrase_overlap: float = 0.0
260	    first_use_after: Optional[timedelta] = None
261	    files_written: int = 0
262	    files_picked_up: int = 0
263	    files_revised: int = 0
264	    files_replaced: int = 0
265	
266	
267	def _report_channel(agent: Agent, parent: Agent) -> Tuple[str, int, int, float, Optional[timedelta]]:
268	    if not agent.report_text:
269	        return "no report", 0, 0, 0.0, None
270	    at = _ts(agent.report_at)
271	    before = [t for ts, t in parent.outputs if _ts(ts) < at]
272	    after = [(ts, t) for ts, t in parent.outputs if _ts(ts) >= at]
273	    if not after:
274	        return "arrived after parent stopped", 0, 0, 0.0, None
275	    known_text = agent.instructions + "\n" + "\n".join(before)
276	    items = signals(agent.report_text) - signals(known_text)
277	    after_text = "\n".join(t for _, t in after)
278	    reused = {x for x in items if x in after_text}
279	    rep_sh = shingles(agent.report_text) - shingles(agent.instructions)
280	    overlap = len(rep_sh & shingles(after_text)) / len(rep_sh) if rep_sh else 0.0
281	    first_use = None
282	    for ts, t in after:
283	        if any(x in t for x in reused) or (rep_sh and rep_sh & shingles(t)):
284	            if ts and agent.report_at:
285	                first_use = ts - agent.report_at
286	            break
287	    if len(reused) >= 2 or overlap >= 0.05:
288	        status = "used"
289	    elif reused or overlap >= 0.01:
290	        # One reused item or a little phrase overlap. A model-judged check (scripts/judge_lineage.py)
291	        # found this also happens by chance: 2 of 6 reports shown next to a different session's lead got it.
292	        status = "unclear"
293	    else:
294	        status = "no trace found"
295	    return status, len(items), len(reused), overlap, first_use
296	
297	
298	def _file_channel(run: Run, agent: Agent) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
299	    written, picked, revised, replaced = 0, 0, 0, 0
300	    for w in agent.tool_calls:
301	        path = w.input.get("file_path")
302	        if w.name not in WRITE_TOOLS or w.is_error or not isinstance(path, str):
303	            continue
304	        written += 1
305	        base = path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
306	        t = _ts(w.started)
307	        later = [c for a in run.agents.values() if a.id != agent.id for c in a.tool_calls if _ts(c.started) > t]
308	        touched = {c.name for c in later if c.input.get("file_path") == path}
309	        in_command = any(c.name == "Bash" and (path in str(c.input.get("command", "")) or
310	                                                (len(base) >= 5 and base in str(c.input.get("command", ""))))
311	                         for c in later)
312	        picked += bool("Read" in touched or in_command)
313	        revised += bool(touched & {"Edit", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"})
314	        replaced += bool("Write" in touched)
315	    return written, picked, revised, replaced
316	
317	
318	def lineage(run: Run) -> List[Lineage]:
319	    out = []
320	    for agent in run.subagents:
321	        parent = run.agents.get(agent.parent_id or "main")
322	        if parent is None:
323	            continue
324	        rstatus, n_items, n_reused, overlap, first_use = _report_channel(agent, parent)
325	        written, picked, revised, replaced = _file_channel(run, agent)
326	        if rstatus == "used" or picked or revised:
327	            status = "used"
328	        elif written and replaced == written:
329	            status = "replaced by another agent"
330	        elif rstatus == "unclear":
331	            status = "unclear"
332	        elif written:
333	            status = "file left as written"
334	        elif rstatus in ("no report", "arrived after parent stopped"):
335	            status = rstatus
336	        else:
337	            status = "no trace found"
338	        out.append(Lineage(agent, status, rstatus, n_items, n_reused, overlap, first_use,
339	                           written, picked, revised, replaced))
340	    return out
341	
342	
343	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4. file conflicts
344	
345	WRITE_TOOLS = {"Write", "Edit", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"}
346	
347	
348	@dataclass
349	class FileConflict:
350	    path: str
351	    kind: str  # "several writers" or "stale write"
352	    agents: List[str]
353	
354	
355	def file_conflicts(run: Run) -> List[FileConflict]:
356	    writes: Dict[str, List[Tuple[float, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
357	    reads: Dict[str, List[Tuple[float, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
358	    for c in run.tool_calls():
359	        path = c.input.get("file_path") or c.input.get("notebook_path")
360	        if not isinstance(path, str):
361	            continue
362	        if c.name in WRITE_TOOLS and not c.is_error:
363	            writes[path].append((_ts(c.started), c.agent_id))
364	        elif c.name == "Read":
365	            reads[path].append((_ts(c.started), c.agent_id))
366	    out = []
367	    for path, ws in writes.items():
368	        writers = sorted({a for _, a in ws})
369	        if len(writers) < 2:
370	            continue
371	        out.append(FileConflict(path, "several writers", writers))
372	        ws = sorted(ws)
373	        for i, (t_other, other) in enumerate(ws):
374	            for t_mine, me in ws[i + 1:]:
375	                if me == other:
376	                    continue
377	                my_reads = [t for t, a in reads[path] if a == me]
378	                read_before = any(t < t_other for t in my_reads)
379	                reread = any(t_other <= t <= t_mine for t in my_reads)
380	                if read_before and not reread:
381	                    out.append(FileConflict(path, "stale write", [other, me]))
382	    return out
383	
384	
385	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. approvals
386	
387	RISKY_RE = re.compile(
388	    r"\brm\s+-\w*[rf]|\bgit\s+(push|reset|clean|checkout\s+--)|\bsudo\b|\bcurl\b|\bwget\b|"
389	    r"\bnpm\s+publish\b|\bpip3?\s+install\b|\bchmod\b|\bdd\s+if=|\bgh\s+(repo|pr|release)\s+(create|delete|merge)"
390	)
391	
392	
393	# Tools whose "permission decision" is really a person answering the agent, not allowing an action.
394	QUESTION_TOOLS = {"AskUserQuestion"}
395	
396	
397	@dataclass
398	class ApprovalReport:
399	    total: int = 0
400	    by_source: Counter = field(default_factory=Counter)
401	    rejected: int = 0
402	    human: List[Tuple[ToolCall, Optional[float]]] = field(default_factory=list)  # (call, seconds call→result)
403	    answers: List[ToolCall] = field(default_factory=list)  # a person answered a question the agent asked
404	    settings_median: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)  # tool → median seconds when settings allowed it
405	
406	    def quick_risky(self, under_seconds: float = 3.0) -> List[ToolCall]:
407	        """Risky commands a person allowed faster than under_seconds after the call (execution time included)."""
408	        return [c for c, s in self.human if s is not None and s < under_seconds and c.approval
409	                and c.approval.decision == "accept" and RISKY_RE.search(str(c.input.get("command", "")))]
410	
411	
412	def approvals(run: Run, only: Optional[Set[str]] = None) -> ApprovalReport:
413	    """Permission decisions in a run. `only`: count just the calls made in these model requests
414	    (used to skip history a fork or resume copied from another file)."""
415	    rep = ApprovalReport()
416	    settings_waits: Dict[str, List[float]] = defaultdict(list)
417	    for c in run.tool_calls():
418	        a = c.approval
419	        if a is None or (only is not None and c.request_id not in only):
420	            continue
421	        rep.total += 1
422	        rep.by_source[a.source] += 1
423	        rep.rejected += a.decision != "accept"
424	        secs = (c.finished - c.started).total_seconds() if c.finished and c.started else None
425	        if a.by_human and c.name in QUESTION_TOOLS:
426	            rep.answers.append(c)
427	        elif a.by_human:
428	            rep.human.append((c, secs))
429	        elif secs is not None:
430	            settings_waits[c.name].append(secs)
431	    rep.settings_median = {k: statistics.median(v) for k, v in settings_waits.items()}
432	    return rep
433	
434	
435	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. parallelism
436	
437	def peak_parallel(run: Run) -> int:
438	    """Most subagents running at the same moment."""
439	    edges = []
440	    for a in run.subagents:
441	        start, end = a.started, a.report_at or a.ended
442	        if start and end and end >= start:
443	            edges += [(_ts(start), 1), (_ts(end), -1)]
444	    peak = cur = 0
445	    for _, d in sorted(edges, key=lambda e: (e[0], e[1])):
446	        cur += d
447	        peak = max(peak, cur)
448	    return peak
449	
450	
451	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- everything for one run
452	
453	def summarize(run: Run, scale: TokenScale, only_owned: bool = False) -> dict:
454	    """All findings for one run. only_owned: leave out history copied from an older file,
455	    so that summing over many runs counts each call once."""
456	    owned_ids = {r.id for r in run.requests() if r.owned or not only_owned}
457	    reqs = [r for r in run.requests() if r.id in owned_ids]
458	    costs = [request_cost(r) for r in reqs]
459	    by_agent_cost: Counter = Counter()
460	    for r, c in zip(reqs, costs):
461	        by_agent_cost["lead" if r.agent_id == "main" else "sub"] += c or 0.0
462	    return {
463	        "run": run,
464	        "cost": sum(c or 0.0 for c in costs),
465	        "cost_unknown": sum(1 for c in costs if c is None),
466	        "lead_cost": by_agent_cost["lead"],
467	        "sub_cost": by_agent_cost["sub"],
468	        "startup": [s for s in startup_costs(run)
469	                    if not only_owned or all(r.id in owned_ids for r in s.agent.requests)],
470	        "repeats": [x for x in find_repeats(run, scale) if x.call.request_id in owned_ids],
471	        "lineage": lineage(run),
472	        "conflicts": file_conflicts(run),
473	        "approvals": approvals(run, owned_ids if only_owned else None),
474	        "peak": peak_parallel(run),
475	    }

1	"""The run model: a clean description of one multi-agent run.
2	
3	Nothing here knows about Claude Code's file format. The adapter in
4	claude_code.py fills these objects in, and everything else only reads them.
5	That way a format change in Claude Code means fixing one file.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	from collections import Counter
11	from dataclasses import dataclass, field, fields
12	from datetime import datetime
13	from typing import Dict, Iterator, List, Optional, Set, Tuple
14	
15	
16	@dataclass
17	class Usage:
18	    """Token counts for one or more model calls.
19	
20	    input        fresh input, billed at full price
21	    cache_write  input stored in the prompt cache on this call (billed a bit above full price)
22	    cache_read   input served from the prompt cache (billed at a small fraction)
23	    output       tokens the model wrote, thinking included
24	    thinking     the thinking part of output, when Claude Code reports it
25	    """
26	
27	    input: int = 0
28	    cache_write: int = 0
29	    cache_read: int = 0
30	    output: int = 0
31	    thinking: int = 0
32	    web_searches: int = 0
33	    web_fetches: int = 0
34	    cache_write_1h: int = 0  # the part of cache_write kept for 1 hour (priced higher than 5-minute writes)
35	
36	    def add(self, other: "Usage") -> "Usage":
37	        for f in fields(self):
38	            setattr(self, f.name, getattr(self, f.name) + getattr(other, f.name))
39	        return self
40	
41	    def max_with(self, other: "Usage") -> "Usage":
42	        """Field-wise maximum. Used when one call is written as several lines."""
43	        return Usage(**{f.name: max(getattr(self, f.name), getattr(other, f.name)) for f in fields(self)})
44	
45	    @property
46	    def total_input(self) -> int:
47	        return self.input + self.cache_write + self.cache_read
48	
49	    @property
50	    def total(self) -> int:
51	        return self.total_input + self.output
52	
53	    def core(self) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
54	        """The four counts Claude Code also keeps in its own totals."""
55	        return (self.input, self.cache_write, self.cache_read, self.output)
56	
57	
58	@dataclass
59	class Approval:
60	    """A permission decision about one tool call."""
61	
62	    tool_use_id: str
63	    decision: str  # "accept" or "reject"
64	    source: str  # "config" = allowed by settings or mode; "user_*" = a person clicked
65	    reason: Optional[str] = None
66	    at: Optional[datetime] = None
67	
68	    @property
69	    def by_human(self) -> bool:
70	        return self.source.startswith("user")
71	
72	
73	@dataclass
74	class ToolCall:
75	    """One tool call an agent made (read a file, run a command, start a subagent...)."""
76	
77	    id: str
78	    agent_id: str
79	    request_id: Optional[str]
80	    name: str
81	    input: dict
82	    started: Optional[datetime] = None
83	    finished: Optional[datetime] = None
84	    is_error: bool = False
85	    result_chars: int = 0
86	    result_hash: Optional[str] = None  # fingerprint of the whole result: equal hashes = identical results
87	    result_media: bool = False  # the result holds images or documents, whose token size we can't measure
88	    approval: Optional[Approval] = None
89	    spawned_agent_id: Optional[str] = None
90	
91	
92	@dataclass
93	class Request:
94	    """One call to the model, however many lines it took in the transcript."""
95	
96	    id: str
97	    agent_id: str
98	    model: str
99	    started: Optional[datetime]
100	    ended: Optional[datetime]
101	    usage: Usage
102	    stop_reason: Optional[str] = None
103	    tool_use_ids: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
104	    shared_with: Set[str] = field(default_factory=set)  # other session files holding the same call
105	    owned: bool = True  # False when another file holds the original of this (copied) call
106	    speed: Optional[str] = None  # "fast" when fast mode was used (priced higher)
107	
108	
109	@dataclass
110	class Event:
111	    """One step in an agent's timeline, in file order.
112	
113	    kind: "call"    a model call (ref = request id)
114	          "result"  a tool result came back (ref = tool call id, chars = its size)
115	          "context" anything else added to the conversation: a message, a
116	                    report from a subagent, a reminder (chars = size, -1 if unknown)
117	    """
118	
119	    kind: str
120	    at: Optional[datetime]
121	    ref: Optional[str] = None
122	    chars: int = 0
123	
124	
125	@dataclass
126	class Agent:
127	    """The lead agent ("main") or one subagent."""
128	
129	    id: str
130	    parent_id: Optional[str]
131	    kind: str  # "lead" for the main agent, else the subagent type
132	    description: str = ""
133	    instructions: str = ""  # the prompt its parent wrote for it
134	    model_requested: Optional[str] = None
135	    spawn_tool_use_id: Optional[str] = None
136	    background: Optional[bool] = None
137	    transcript: Optional[str] = None  # None when the subagent left no transcript file
138	    requests: List[Request] = field(default_factory=list)
139	    tool_calls: List[ToolCall] = field(default_factory=list)
140	    started: Optional[datetime] = None
141	    ended: Optional[datetime] = None
142	    report_at: Optional[datetime] = None  # when its final report reached the parent
143	    report_chars: int = 0
144	    report_text: str = ""  # kept in memory for lineage; never printed unless asked
145	    outputs: List[Tuple[Optional[datetime], str]] = field(default_factory=list)  # what this agent wrote
146	    said: List[Tuple[Optional[datetime], str]] = field(default_factory=list)  # its plain text messages only
147	    events: List[Event] = field(default_factory=list)
148	
149	    def usage(self) -> Usage:
150	        total = Usage()
151	        for r in self.requests:
152	            total.add(r.usage)
153	        return total
154	
155	    def models(self) -> List[str]:
156	        return sorted({r.model for r in self.requests})
157	
158	    def seen(self, ts: Optional[datetime]) -> None:
159	        if ts is None:
160	            return
161	        if self.started is None or ts < self.started:
162	            self.started = ts
163	        if self.ended is None or ts > self.ended:
164	            self.ended = ts
165	
166	
167	@dataclass
168	class Run:
169	    """One session: the lead agent plus every subagent it started."""
170	
171	    session_id: str
172	    path: str
173	    project: str
174	    title: Optional[str] = None
175	    agents: Dict[str, Agent] = field(default_factory=dict)
176	    human_messages: List[datetime] = field(default_factory=list)
177	    compactions: List[datetime] = field(default_factory=list)
178	    reported_totals: Optional[dict] = None  # Claude Code's own running totals, as recorded
179	    derived_from: List[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
180	    versions: Set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
181	    unknown_record_types: Counter = field(default_factory=Counter)
182	    missing_transcripts: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
183	    bad_lines: int = 0
184	    notes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
185	
186	    @property
187	    def lead(self) -> Agent:
188	        return self.agents["main"]
189	
190	    @property
191	    def subagents(self) -> List[Agent]:
192	        return [a for a in self.agents.values() if a.id != "main"]
193	
194	    @property
195	    def started(self) -> Optional[datetime]:
196	        times = [a.started for a in self.agents.values() if a.started]
197	        return min(times) if times else None
198	
199	    @property
200	    def ended(self) -> Optional[datetime]:
201	        times = [a.ended for a in self.agents.values() if a.ended]
202	        return max(times) if times else None

1	"""Facts that need more than one session file.
2	
3	Claude Code copies history into a new file when a session is forked, resumed
4	or continued. The same model call then appears in several files. This index
5	lets a run say which of its calls also live elsewhere, so copied history is
6	never counted as new spend.
7	
8	Ownership rule: a shared call belongs to the file that was created first. A
9	fork or resume file is always created after the file it copies from. On macOS
10	the file's birth time is used; elsewhere, its first timestamp, then its name.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import json
16	import os
17	from collections import defaultdict
18	from typing import Dict, Optional, Set, Tuple
19	
20	from .claude_code import find_sessions, session_id_of, subagent_files
21	from .model import Run
22	
23	
24	class Corpus:
25	    def __init__(self, root: Optional[str] = None):
26	        self.calls: Dict[str, Set[str]] = defaultdict(set)  # request id -> session ids
27	        self.created: Dict[str, Tuple[float, str, str]] = {}  # session id -> sort key
28	        for path in find_sessions(root):
29	            sid = session_id_of(path)
30	            first_ts = ""
31	            for p in [path] + subagent_files(path):
32	                with open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
33	                    for line in f:
34	                        if not first_ts and '"timestamp"' in line:
35	                            try:
36	                                first_ts = str(json.loads(line).get("timestamp") or "")
37	                            except json.JSONDecodeError:
38	                                pass
39	                        if '"requestId"' not in line:
40	                            continue
41	                        try:
42	                            r = json.loads(line)
43	                        except json.JSONDecodeError:
44	                            continue
45	                        if r.get("type") == "assistant" and r.get("requestId"):
46	                            self.calls[r["requestId"]].add(sid)
47	            st = os.stat(path)
48	            self.created[sid] = (getattr(st, "st_birthtime", 0.0), first_ts, sid)
49	
50	    def owner(self, request_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
51	        sids = self.calls.get(request_id)
52	        if not sids:
53	            return None
54	        return min(sids, key=lambda s: self.created.get(s, (0.0, "", s)))
55	
56	    def mark(self, run: Run) -> None:
57	        for req in run.requests():
58	            sids = self.calls.get(req.id, set())
59	            req.shared_with = set(sids) - {run.session_id}
60	            owner = self.owner(req.id)
61	            req.owned = owner is None or owner == run.session_id
62	
63	
64	def request_index(root: Optional[str] = None) -> Corpus:
65	    """Kept for older callers: returns the Corpus."""
66	    return Corpus(root)

69	def mark_shared(run: Run, corpus: Corpus) -> None:
70	    corpus.mark(run)

1	"""Cross-check our token counts against Claude Code's own totals.
2	
3	Claude Code keeps a running total per session (the cost-state record). A
4	"clean" session shares no calls with other files, was never compacted, and is
5	not still running. For a clean session the rule is:
6	
7	  * we may count LESS than Claude Code, because some calls never reach the
8	    transcript (side calls on other models, and a few small same-model calls
9	    whose purpose we have not identified);
10	  * we must never count MORE. That would mean the reader double-counts.
11	
12	For other sessions we report the gap and the reason.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import os
18	import time
19	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
20	from typing import Dict, List, Optional
21	
22	from .model import Run, Usage
23	
24	FIELDS = {
25	    "input": "inputTokens",
26	    "cache_write": "cacheCreationInputTokens",
27	    "cache_read": "cacheReadInputTokens",
28	    "output": "outputTokens",
29	}
30	LIVE_SECONDS = 15 * 60
31	
32	
33	def reported_by_model(run: Run) -> Dict[str, Usage]:
34	    totals = (run.reported_totals or {}).get("modelUsage") or {}
35	    out = {}
36	    for model, d in totals.items():
37	        if isinstance(d, dict):
38	            out[model] = Usage(**{ours: int(d.get(theirs) or 0) for ours, theirs in FIELDS.items()})
39	    return out
40	
41	
42	@dataclass
43	class ModelCheck:
44	    model: str
45	    ours: Optional[Usage]
46	    theirs: Optional[Usage]
47	
48	    @property
49	    def status(self) -> str:
50	        if self.ours is None:
51	            return "not in transcript"
52	        if self.theirs is None:
53	            return "not in Claude Code's totals"
54	        if self.ours.core() == self.theirs.core():
55	            return "match"
56	        if all(o <= t for o, t in zip(self.ours.core(), self.theirs.core())):
57	            return "transcript missing calls"
58	        return "overcount"
59	
60	    def missing(self) -> Usage:
61	        """Tokens Claude Code counted that the transcript does not show."""
62	        if self.ours is None or self.theirs is None:
63	            return Usage()
64	        return Usage(*(max(t - o, 0) for o, t in zip(self.ours.core(), self.theirs.core())))
65	
66	
67	@dataclass
68	class SessionCheck:
69	    run: Run
70	    models: List[ModelCheck]
71	    shared_calls: int
72	    compactions: int
73	    live: bool
74	    reasons: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
75	
76	    @property
77	    def has_totals(self) -> bool:
78	        return self.run.reported_totals is not None
79	
80	    @property
81	    def clean(self) -> bool:
82	        return self.has_totals and not self.shared_calls and not self.compactions and not self.live
83	
84	    @property
85	    def transcript_models_match(self) -> bool:
86	        seen = [m for m in self.models if m.ours is not None]
87	        return bool(seen) and all(m.status == "match" for m in seen)
88	
89	    @property
90	    def side_models(self) -> List[ModelCheck]:
91	        return [m for m in self.models if m.status == "not in transcript"]
92	
93	    @property
94	    def verdict(self) -> str:
95	        if not self.has_totals:
96	            return "no totals recorded"
97	        if not any(m.ours is not None for m in self.models):
98	            return "no model calls"
99	        if self.transcript_models_match:
100	            return "match"
101	        if not self.clean:
102	            return "differs (explained)"
103	        statuses = {m.status for m in self.models if m.ours is not None}
104	        if "overcount" in statuses or "not in Claude Code's totals" in statuses:
105	            return "OVERCOUNT"
106	        return "transcript missing calls"
107	
108	
109	def check_run(run: Run, now: Optional[float] = None) -> SessionCheck:
110	    now = time.time() if now is None else now
111	    ours = run.usage_by_model()
112	    theirs = reported_by_model(run)
113	    models = [ModelCheck(m, ours.get(m), theirs.get(m)) for m in sorted(set(ours) | set(theirs))]
114	    shared = sum(1 for r in run.requests() if r.shared_with)
115	    live = (now - os.path.getmtime(run.path)) < LIVE_SECONDS if os.path.exists(run.path) else False
116	    result = SessionCheck(run=run, models=models, shared_calls=shared, compactions=len(run.compactions), live=live)
117	    if shared:
118	        others = {s for r in run.requests() for s in r.shared_with}
119	        result.reasons.append(f"{shared} calls also in {len(others)} other file(s) (fork/resume copies)")
120	    if run.compactions:
121	        result.reasons.append(f"{len(run.compactions)} compaction(s); summarizing calls are not in the transcript")
122	    if live:
123	        result.reasons.append("still running; Claude Code's totals lag")
124	    return result

170	    """Estimate: was handing the job to a subagent cheaper than the lead doing it itself?

173	    the rest of its calls.
174	    Inline (estimate): the lead makes the same calls itself, at its own prices, on
175	    top of the context it already had when it started the subagent; the subagent's
176	    context growth (everything it read and wrote after its first call) then stays
177	    in the lead's context for the rest of the lead's calls.
178	
179	    Assumptions: the lead would take the same steps; report size uses the measured
180	    characters-per-token ratio of tool results, which overstates prose a little and so
181	    favours the inline side.

183	    Two bounds, because Claude Code can compact or clear old context:
184	      keep  the material stays in the lead's context for all its later calls (upper bound

207	        inline_work = 0.0
208	        for i, q in enumerate(reqs):
209	            growth = max(0, q.usage.total_input - base)
210	            new = 0 if i == 0 else q.usage.input + q.usage.cache_write
211	            inline_work += (lead_ctx + growth - new) * r_ + new * w + q.usage.output * o
212	        growth_total = max(0, reqs[-1].usage.total_input + reqs[-1].usage.output - base)

221	            "growth_tokens": growth_total, "lead_context": lead_ctx, "same_model": az.main_model(a) == model,
222	            "inline": inline, "delegated": sub_cost + carry_report,
223	            "delegated_at_lead_prices": sub_cost_lead_prices + carry_report,
224	            "inline_drop": inline_work, "delegated_drop": sub_cost + write_report,
225	            "delegated_drop_at_lead_prices": sub_cost_lead_prices + write_report,
226	        })
227	    cheaper = [x for x in rows if x["delegated"] < x["inline"]]
228	    cheaper_same = [x for x in rows if x["delegated_at_lead_prices"] < x["inline"]]
229	    small = [x for x in rows if x["calls"] <= 5]

250	def fanouts(ds: Dataset) -> List[List[Agent]]:
251	    """Groups of subagents with the same parent started within FANOUT_WINDOW seconds of the group's first."""

The `claude_code.py` header also says it is "the only file that knows Claude Code's on-disk format."

2. **`docs/learn/02-what-a-token-costs.md`**: "I didn't copy a price list." `src/flightrec/pricing.py` (lines 7–8) says the table is "from Anthropic's published list (Nov 2026)." The doc's Opus prices ($4, $5, $8, $0.20, $20) and the 2x fast-mode multiplier do match `PRICES` and `FAST_MODE_MULTIPLIER` in that file.

3. **`docs/learn/02-what-a-token-costs.md`**: "Claude Code saves its own dollar cost next to its token counts, so I worked backwards from those records," and "reproduce Claude Code's recorded cost to the cent in 37 of 38 Opus records" and "match Claude Code's to the cent in all 12 clean sessions." No code in `src/flightrec` reads a recorded dollar cost. `claude_code.py` parses no cost field, and `check.py` (`FIELDS`, lines 24–29) compares tokens only. In `analyze.py` `_report_channel`, the item channel subtracts the parent's earlier text (line 275, `signals(known_text)`). The phrase channel subtracts only the instructions (line 279), and `overlap` (line 280) and `first_use` (line 283) match against the parent's full later text. So a phrase the lead already had can push a report to "used" through the `overlap >= 0.05` test at line 287. The `analyze.py` module docstring (lines 240–252) says "exact phrases the parent didn't already have," which is also not what the code does.
